To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cancer cachexia is accompanied by a decrease of body adipose tissue mass, a decrease of body weight in proportion to tumour mass, and a decrease of liver mass in proportion to body weight, and that the liberated fatty acids are taken-up both by tumour and liver.
cancer cachexia is accompanied by a mobilization of adipocytes reserves and that the liberated fatty acids are taken-up by the tumour.
the growth of a transplantable murine tumour is accompanied by a decrease of body weight in the host and an increased uptake of essential fatty acids by the host and the tumour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of essential fatty acids in the pathophysiology of cancer cachexia.
the role of the liver as an intermediary between adipose tissue and tumour in the regulation of the availability of fatty acids for tumor growth in an experimental cachectic model.
the effects of tumour growth on host lipid metabolism and the effect of weight loss on the lipid metabolism of the tumour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fatty acid composition of tumours and host tissues changes in response to the tumour growth and that these changes may be of importance for the tumour growth.
cancer cachexia is associated with a mobilization of adipocytes, which in turn leads to an increase of fatty acid concentration in plasma, which is then taken-up by the liver and the tumour.
the fatty acid metabolism in tumour-bearing mice is altered in a way which favours tumour growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tumour is able to utilize fatty acids for growth and this utilization increases with increasing weight loss.
fatty acids play an important role in the development of cancer cachexia.
the tumours were able to utilize fatty acids from the host and that these fatty acids were essential for tumour growth and development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is the major organ for fatty acid metabolism and accumulation in the cachectic host.
the tumour can use fatty acids from the host for its own growth.
the fatty acid composition of tumour tissue is determined by the fatty acid composition and availability in the host.
